new_note: *And all the sons of Adam assembled and came to Enoch that day; and all the kings of the earth with their princes and counsellors remained with him that day; and Enoch then taught the sons of men wisdom and knowledge, and gave them divine instruction; and he bade them serve Yahuah (the Lord) and walk in his ways all the days of their lives, and he continued to make peace amongst them.* (Jasher 3:31). *And on account of it Elohim (God) brought the waters of the flood upon all the land of Eden; for there he was set as a sign and that he should testify against all the children of men, that he should recount all the deeds of the generations until the day of condemnation.* (Jubilees 4:24). Jubilees tells why Enoch was taken: he was set as a sign against all the children of men, to recount the deeds of every generation until the day of condemnation. Jasher shows him doing that very work on his last day among them, gathering the sons of Adam and the kings of the earth, teaching them wisdom and knowledge, and bidding them serve Yahuah (the Lord) and walk in his ways. The witness who will testify against the generations first pleaded with them to walk right while he was still in reach.
member_note: Jasher 3:31 — *he bade them serve Yahuah (the Lord) and walk in his ways all the days of their lives.* Enoch's last day of teaching before he was taken is the witness Jubilees says he was set apart to bear.

new_note: *And it was after this that Yahuah (the Lord) said to Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me, on account of their evil deeds, and behold I will destroy the earth.* (Jasher 5:25). *And Elohim (God) said unto Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me; for the earth is filled with violence through them; and, behold, I will destroy them with the earth.* (Genesis 6:13). Jasher carries the decree of Genesis nearly word for word: the end of all flesh is come before me, and behold I will destroy the earth. Where Genesis names the cause as violence filling the earth, Jasher names it as their evil deeds, and the two are one charge told by two witnesses. The same Yahuah (the Lord) who spoke to Noah speaks in both records, and the judgment on all flesh is settled before the ark is ever named.
member_note: Jasher 5:25 — *The end of all flesh is come before me, on account of their evil deeds.* Jasher gives the decree of Genesis 6:13 to Noah nearly word for word before the command to build the ark.

new_note: *And all the fountains of the deep were broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened, and the rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights.* (Jasher 6:14). *And Yahuah (God) opened seven flood-gates of heaven, And the mouths of the fountains of the great deep, seven mouths in number.* (Jubilees 5:24). Both witnesses open the flood from above and from beneath at once. Jasher says the fountains of the deep were broken up and the windows of heaven were opened; Jubilees counts them, seven flood-gates of heaven and seven mouths of the great deep. The rain of forty days and forty nights in Jasher is the same water Jubilees watches Yahuah (God) release by his own hand, so the flood is not weather but judgment ordered from the throne.
member_note: Jasher 6:14 — *all the fountains of the deep were broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened.* Jubilees 5:24 counts the same fountains and flood-gates Jasher reports being opened.

new_note: *And Elohim (God) remembered Noah, and every living thing, and all the cattle that was with him in the ark: and Elohim (God) made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters asswaged;* (Genesis 8:1). *And a wind passed over the earth, and the waters were still and the ark rested.* (Jasher 6:33). Jasher stands almost word for word beside the Torah here, and it binds three things into one moment: the wind passes, the waters grow still, and the ark comes to rest. Genesis adds the cause the reader needs, that Elohim (God) remembered Noah, and that remembering is what sends the wind. The breath that moves over the deep and quiets it is the same breath that moved over the waters in the beginning; the flood ends the way the world began, with Elohim (God) ordering the deep by his Spirit.
member_note: Jasher 6:33 — *And a wind passed over the earth, and the waters were still and the ark rested.* Jasher binds the wind, the stilling of the waters, and the resting of the ark into the one moment Genesis 8:1 describes.

new_note: *And they went and returned every one to his way and to his place, and Noah and his sons dwelt in the land that Elohim had told them, and they served Yahuah (the Lord) all their days, and Yahuah (the Lord) blessed Noah and his sons on their going out from the ark.* (Jasher 6:41). *And Yahuah (LORD) smelled a sweet savour; and Yahuah (LORD) said in his heart, I will not again curse the ground any more for man’s sake; for the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth; neither will I again smite any more every thing living, as I have done.* (Genesis 8:21). Genesis records what Yahuah (LORD) said in his heart after the flood, that he would not again curse the ground nor again smite every living thing, and Jasher records what that mercy looked like on the ground: Noah and his sons dwelt where Elohim (God) told them, served Yahuah (the Lord) all their days, and were blessed by him on their going out from the ark. The promise never to repeat the flood and the blessing on the family that came out of it are one kindness, spoken over the same ground on the same day the ark was emptied.
member_note: Jasher 6:41 — *they served Yahuah (the Lord) all their days, and Yahuah (the Lord) blessed Noah and his sons.* The blessing on Noah's house at the going out from the ark is the mercy Genesis 8:21 records Yahuah (LORD) resolving in his heart.
flag: The old note placed Noah's altar in Jasher 6:41, but the live Jasher verse (and its neighbours) says nothing of an altar; it has Noah's family serving Yahuah and being blessed on leaving the ark. I wrote the connection from what the verse actually says. Thread slug is jasher-6-altar-covenant-bow; the author may want to check that thread's framing.

new_note: *And he said to them, Be fruitful and fill all the earth; become strong and increase abundantly in the earth and multiply in it.* (Jasher 6:42). *"And you, increase you and multiply upon the earth, and become many upon it, and be a blessing upon it. The fear of you and the dread of you I shall inspire in everything that is on earth and in the sea.* (Jubilees 6:5). Jubilees gives the same charge in the same breath: increase, multiply upon the earth, become many upon it, and be a blessing upon it. Jasher's be fruitful and fill all the earth, become strong and increase abundantly, is one command heard by two witnesses, spoken by Yahuah (the Lord) to the same eight souls on the same day they came out of the ark. The earth emptied by judgment is handed back to Noah's house to fill.
member_note: Jasher 6:42 — *Be fruitful and fill all the earth; become strong and increase abundantly in the earth.* Jubilees 6:5 carries the same charge to multiply and be a blessing that Jasher gives Noah's sons at the ark.
flag: Live Jubilees 6:5 text begins with a stray opening double-quote mark and is quoted as it stands; the author may want to clean the source text.

new_note: *And when all the wise men and conjurors went out from the house of Terah, they lifted up their eyes toward heaven that night to look at the stars, and they saw, and behold one very large star came from the east and ran in the heavens, and he swallowed up the four stars from the four sides of the heavens.* (Jasher 8:2). *Now when Yahusha (Jesus) was born in Bethlehem of Judaea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem,* (Matthew 2:1). On the night Abram is born, Nimrod's wise men look up from Terah's house and see one great star run across the heavens and swallow four others, and they understand its import; before the chapter is out Nimrod is demanding the child's life. On the night Yahusha (Jesus) is born, wise men from the east read the heavens the same way and come to Jerusalem, and Herod moves to kill the child. Twice the sky announces the seed of promise at its birth, and twice the kingdom of man answers by reaching for the infant. What happened to Abram is what happened to the Messiah (Christ), because it is one war against one seed.
member_note: Jasher 8:2 — *behold one very large star came from the east and ran in the heavens.* The star Nimrod's wise men read at Abram's birth is answered by the star Herod's wise men follow at the birth of Yahusha (Jesus).

new_note: *And Terah took his son Abram and his grandson Lot, the son of Haran, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, the wife of his son Abram, and all the souls of his household and went with them from Ur Casdim to go to the land of Canaan. And when they came as far as the land of Haran they remained there, for it was exceedingly good land for pasture, and of sufficient extent for those who accompanied them.* (Jasher 13:1). *Then came he out of the land of the Chaldæans, and dwelt in Charran: and from thence, when his father was dead, he removed him into this land, wherein ye now dwell.* (Acts 7:4). Stephen tells the route in one sentence, out of the land of the Chaldaeans, a stay in Charran, and then into the land after his father died, and Jasher walks it step by step: Terah takes Abram, Lot, and Sarai out of Ur Casdim meaning to reach Canaan, and the household stops in Haran because the pasture is good. Both witnesses agree that Haran was never the destination, only the pause, and that the call to Canaan was already in motion when Terah's household left Ur. Stephen tells in one sentence the journey Jasher tells step by step, and the two do not differ.
member_note: Jasher 13:1 — *went with them from Ur Casdim to go to the land of Canaan.* Terah's household leaving Ur for Canaan and stopping in Haran is the route Stephen gives in Acts 7:4.

new_note: *And now therefore if you will hearken to my voice and keep my commandments, my statutes and my laws, then will I cause your enemies to fall before you, and I will multiply your seed like the stars of heaven, and I will send my blessing upon all the works of your hands, and you shall lack nothing.* (Jasher 13:4). *And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be.* (Genesis 15:5). Genesis gives the promise under the open sky: look toward heaven, count the stars, so shall your seed be. Jasher gives the same promise in Haran with its condition spoken out loud: if you will hearken to my voice and keep my commandments, my statutes and my laws, then I will multiply your seed like the stars of heaven. The multiplying of the seed and the keeping of his ways are never two separate matters in the mouth of Yahuah (the Lord); the promise is sure, and it is walked in by obedience. What Genesis shows Abram believing, Jasher shows him being told to keep.
member_note: Jasher 13:4 — *I will multiply your seed like the stars of heaven.* The seed numbered like the stars in Genesis 15:5 is spoken in Jasher together with the call to keep his commandments.

new_note: *And Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to Abram when he came to the land of Canaan, and said to him, This is the land which I gave to you and to your seed after you forever, and I will make your seed like the stars of heaven, and I will give to your seed for an inheritance all the lands which you see.* (Jasher 13:7). *And Yahuah (LORD) appeared unto Abram, and said, Unto thy seed will I give this land: and there builded he an altar unto Yahuah (LORD), who appeared unto him.* (Genesis 12:7). Both witnesses place the same word at the same spot: Abram arrives in Canaan, Yahuah (LORD) appears to him, and the land is given to his seed. Genesis says it in a line and then shows Abram building the altar; Jasher opens the word out, this land to you and to your seed after you forever, your seed like the stars of heaven, all the lands which you see for an inheritance, and then in its next verse Abram builds the same altar and calls on the same name. The gift of the land to the seed is spoken at the threshold, before Abram owns a single field in it.
member_note: Jasher 13:7 — *This is the land which I gave to you and to your seed after you forever.* Yahuah (the Lord) appearing to Abram on his entry into Canaan and giving the land to his seed is the word of Genesis 12:7.

new_note: *And Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to Abram when he came to the land of Canaan, and said to him, This is the land which I gave to you and to your seed after you forever, and I will make your seed like the stars of heaven, and I will give to your seed for an inheritance all the lands which you see.* (Jasher 13:7). *For all the land which thou seest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever.* (Genesis 13:15). Genesis 13 has Abram lift his eyes and hear that all the land he sees is given to him and to his seed forever, and Jasher gathers that same word into the first appearing at Abram's entry into Canaan: I will give to your seed for an inheritance all the lands which you see. The measure of the gift is the reach of Abram's own eyes, and the term of it is forever. Two witnesses, one promise, and no later covenant takes back a yard of it.
member_note: Jasher 13:7 — *I will give to your seed for an inheritance all the lands which you see.* All the land Abram sees given to his seed forever is the word of Genesis 13:15 spoken in Jasher at his entry into Canaan.

new_note: *Go forth from your land, from your birth-place and from your father’s house, to the land which I have shown you to give it to you and to your children, for there in that land will I bless you, and make you a great nation, and make your name great, and in you shall the families of the earth be blessed.* (Jasher 13:23). *And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.* (Genesis 12:3). Jasher has Yahuah (the Lord) remind Abram in Haran of what he said twenty years before, and the closing clause is the one Genesis preserves: in you shall the families of the earth be blessed. Jasher also keeps the going out from land and birth-place and father's house, the great nation, and the great name, so the whole call of Genesis 12 stands in this one verse. The blessing on the families of the earth runs through Abram and his seed; it is not spread out apart from them, it is carried by them.
member_note: Jasher 13:23 — *in you shall the families of the earth be blessed.* The blessing on all families of the earth from Genesis 12:3 is kept in Jasher's recall of Abram's call in Haran.

new_note: *And now therefore behold, here is all belonging to you, take it and go; as Yahuah (the Lord) lives I will not take from you from a living soul down to a shoetie or thread, excepting the expense of the food of those who went out with me to battle, as also the portions of the men who went with me, Anar, Ashcol, and Mamre, they and their men, as well as those also who had remained to watch the baggage, they shall take their portion of the spoil.* (Jasher 16:16). *And Abram said to him: “I lift up my hands to the El Elyon (Most High) Elohim (God), that from a thread to a shoe-latchet I shall not take aught that is your, lest you should say I have made Abram rich; save only what the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who went with me–Aner, Eschol, and Mamre. These will take their portion.”* (Jubilees 13:29). Jubilees and Jasher give the same oath in nearly the same words. Abram will not take from Sodom's king so much as a thread or a shoe-latchet, Jubilees says, lest it be said that man made Abram rich; Jasher has him swear as Yahuah (the Lord) lives that he will take nothing from a living soul down to a shoetie or thread. Both keep the same exceptions, what the young men ate and the portions of Anar, Ashcol, and Mamre. Abram's riches had just been promised him by Yahuah his Elohim (the Lord his God) in the verse before, and he would not let Sodom claim the credit.
member_note: Jasher 16:16 — *I will not take from you from a living soul down to a shoetie or thread.* Abram's oath to take nothing of Sodom's spoil is the same thread and shoe-latchet refusal Jubilees 13:29 records.

new_note: *And the child grew up and he was weaned, and Abraham made a great feast upon the day that Isaac was weaned.* (Jasher 21:4). *And the child grew, and was weaned: and Abraham made a great feast the same day that Isaac was weaned.* (Genesis 21:8). Jasher retells the Genesis verse almost word for word: the child grew, he was weaned, and Abraham made a great feast on the day of the weaning. Where Genesis stops, Jasher goes on in its next verse to name who came, Shem and Eber and the great people of the land and Abimelech with Phicol, so the feast of Isaac's weaning is a gathering of the kept line and the kings around it. The son of promise is celebrated in the open before all of them.
member_note: Jasher 21:4 — *Abraham made a great feast upon the day that Isaac was weaned.* Jasher retells the great weaning feast of Genesis 21:8 and then names the guests who came to it.

new_note: *And she bare to him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuach, being six sons. And the children of Zimran were Abihen, Molich and Narim.* (Jasher 25:2). *And Abraham took to himself a third wife, and her name was Keturah, from among the daughters of his household servants, for Hagar had died before Sarah.* (Jubilees 19:11). Jubilees records Abraham taking Keturah as a third wife after Hagar had died, and Jasher gives the six sons she bore him, Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuach, and then goes further into their children. The two records sit side by side on the same household in Abraham's old age. Jasher's naming of the grandsons shows how far the sons of Keturah spread, and Genesis will say Abraham gave them gifts and sent them away from Isaac, so the seed of promise and the other sons of Abraham are kept distinct from the start.
member_note: Jasher 25:2 — *she bare to him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuach, being six sons.* Keturah's six sons in Jasher stand beside Jubilees 19:11, which records Abraham taking her as his third wife.
flag: The old note quoted Jubilees 19:11–12, but the card's other end is 19:11 alone and only that verse's text was supplied, so I quoted 19:11 only.

new_note: *And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males.* (Genesis 34:25). *And Simeon and Levi swore and said, As Yahuah (the Lord) lives, the Elohim (God) of the whole earth, by this time tomorrow, there shall not be a remnant left in the whole city.* (Jasher 34:23). Genesis gives the deed, Simeon and Levi taking each man his sword on the third day and slaying all the males, and Jasher gives the oath that stood behind it the day before: as Yahuah (the Lord) lives, by this time tomorrow there shall not be a remnant left in the whole city. The vow is total, and it is sworn in the name of the Elohim (God) of the whole earth, which makes the deed heavier, not lighter. Jacob was filled with wrath when he heard it, and on his deathbed he will curse their anger, so the record keeps their fierceness as a warning, never as a pattern.
member_note: Jasher 34:23 — *by this time tomorrow, there shall not be a remnant left in the whole city.* The oath Simeon and Levi swear in Jasher is carried out in the slaughter of Genesis 34:25.

new_note: *And all the inhabitants of the city of Sarton were powerful men, one of them would pursue a thousand, and two of them would not flee from ten thousand of the rest of men.* (Jasher 38:50). *How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, except their Rock had sold them, and Yahuah (LORD) had shut them up?* (Deuteronomy 32:30). Jasher measures the men of Sarton by the same yardstick Moses sings: one chasing a thousand, two standing against ten thousand. Yet the song asks how one could chase a thousand unless their Rock had sold them and Yahuah (LORD) had shut them up, and that is exactly what the next verse of Jasher shows, the sons of Jacob slaying those mighty men with the edge of the sword and no man standing against them. Strength that could rout a thousand fell in a day, because the hand that gives such strength can shut it up.
member_note: Jasher 38:50 — *one of them would pursue a thousand, and two of them would not flee from ten thousand.* The one who chases a thousand in Deuteronomy 32:30 is the measure Jasher gives the men of Sarton before the sons of Jacob slay them.

new_note: *And Judah took the swords which had fallen from their hands, and Judah fought with them and slew twenty of their men upon the wall.* (Jasher 39:34). *Yahudah (Judah), thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies; thy father’s children shall bow down before thee.* (Genesis 49:8). Jacob's blessing says Yahudah's (Judah's) hand shall be in the neck of his enemies, and Jasher shows what that looks like before the blessing is ever spoken: the men on the wall drop their swords at his shout, and Yahudah (Judah) takes up the fallen swords and slays twenty of them where they stand. The next verse of Jasher says Yahuah (the Lord) put the fear of Yahudah (Judah) in their hearts, so the hand on the enemy's neck is Yahuah's (the Lord's) doing through him. The lion of the blessing is already on the wall.
member_note: Jasher 39:34 — *Judah took the swords which had fallen from their hands, and Judah fought with them.* Yahudah (Judah) slaying twenty men with their own fallen swords is the hand in the neck of his enemies that Genesis 49:8 foretells.

new_note: *And Yahuah (the Lord) was with Joseph and he became a prosperous man, and Yahuah (the Lord) blessed the house of Potiphar for the sake of Joseph.* (Jasher 44:12). *And it came to pass from the time that he had made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, that Yahuah (LORD) blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake; and the blessing of Yahuah (LORD) was upon all that he had in the house, and in the field.* (Genesis 39:5). Jasher retells the Genesis verse in a sentence: Yahuah (the Lord) was with Joseph, he prospered, and the house of Potiphar was blessed for his sake. Genesis spells out the reach of it, upon all that Potiphar had in the house and in the field, from the day Joseph was made overseer. The blessing does not stop at the man Yahuah (the Lord) is with; it spills over onto the house that holds him, even the house of a stranger that holds him as a slave.
member_note: Jasher 44:12 — *Yahuah (the Lord) blessed the house of Potiphar for the sake of Joseph.* Jasher retells Genesis 39:5, where Potiphar's whole house is blessed for Joseph's sake.

new_note: *And it came to pass from the time that he had made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, that Yahuah (LORD) blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake; and the blessing of Yahuah (LORD) was upon all that he had in the house, and in the field.* (Genesis 39:5). *And Yahuah (the Lord) was with Joseph and he became a prosperous man, and Yahuah (the Lord) blessed the house of Potiphar for the sake of Joseph.* (Jasher 44:12). Genesis says the Egyptian's house was blessed for Joseph's sake, and the blessing of Yahuah (LORD) lay on all he had in the house and in the field; Jasher keeps it whole in one line, Yahuah (the Lord) was with Joseph and blessed the house of Potiphar for the sake of Joseph. The presence that went down with him into slavery did not wait for his freedom to start working. Where the one Yahuah (the Lord) favours dwells, the blessing overflows onto the house that holds him.
member_note: Jasher 44:12 — *Yahuah (the Lord) was with Joseph and he became a prosperous man.* Jasher keeps the blessing on Potiphar's house for Joseph's sake whole beside Genesis 39:5.

new_note: *And Joseph was afraid of her at her doing this thing, and he rose up to flee from her, and she seized the front of his garments, and in the terror of his flight the garment which Zelicah seized was torn, and Joseph left the garment in the hand of Zelicah, and he fled and got out, for he was in fear.* (Jasher 44:54). *But she embraced him and held him fast in the house in order to force him to lie with her, and closed the doors of the house and held him fast; but he left his garment in her hands and broke through the door and fled without from her presence.* (Jubilees 39:9). Jubilees and Jasher keep the same ending to the same scene: the garment left in her hands and Joseph fleeing from her presence. Jubilees has her close the doors and hold him fast until he breaks through and runs; Jasher has her seize the front of his garments so that it tears in the terror of his flight. Both put the torn garment in her hand, which is the very thing she will turn into a false witness against him in the verses that follow. The evidence of his innocence becomes the tool of his accusation.
member_note: Jasher 44:54 — *Joseph left the garment in the hand of Zelicah, and he fled and got out.* The garment left in Potiphar's wife's hand as Joseph flees is kept by Jubilees 39:9 as well.

new_note: *And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar; and Phares begat Esrom; and Esrom begat Aram;* (Matthew 1:3). *And in those days Judah went to the house of Shem and took Tamar the daughter of Elam, the son of Shem, for a wife for his first born Er.* (Jasher 45:23). Matthew puts Thamar in the line of the Messiah (Christ), and Jasher tells where Yahudah (Judah) found her: in the house of Shem, the daughter of Elam the son of Shem. She is not a Canaanite brought in from outside; she is a daughter of Shem's own house, inside the kept line from Noah, and her sons Phares and Zara are of that seed on both sides. The women named in Matthew 1 are there to show the seed of promise being guarded, not strangers being added to it, and Jasher 45 is the witness that settles where Tamar came from.
member_note: Jasher 45:23 — *took Tamar the daughter of Elam, the son of Shem, for a wife for his first born Er.* Jasher places Tamar in the house of Shem, so the Thamar of Matthew 1:3 is a daughter of the kept line, not a Canaanite.
flag: The old note quoted the Jasher verse with 'Yahudah (Judah)' inserted; the live Jasher text reads 'Judah' and is quoted as it stands.

new_note: *And Joseph said to him, The three baskets which you did see are three days, yet within three days Pharaoh will take off your head, and hang you upon a tree, and the birds will eat your flesh from off you, as you saw in your dream.* (Jasher 46:14). *Yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and shall hang thee on a tree; and the birds shall eat thy flesh from off thee.* (Genesis 40:19). Joseph's verdict on the baker runs the same in both records: within three days Pharaoh will take his head, hang him on a tree, and the birds will eat his flesh. Jasher adds only the reading of the three baskets as three days, which Genesis gives in the verse before. The dream that promised the butler his place promised the baker a tree, and Joseph told each man the truth of his own dream without softening it.
member_note: Jasher 46:14 — *within three days Pharaoh will take off your head, and hang you upon a tree.* Joseph's verdict that the baker will hang on a tree is the word of Genesis 40:19.

new_note: *And Isaac called Jacob and his sons, and they all came and sat before Isaac, and Isaac said to Jacob, Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) of the whole earth said to me, To your seed will I give this land for an inheritance if your children keep my statutes and my ways, and I will perform to them the oath which I swore to your father Abraham.* (Jasher 47:7). *Sojourn in this land, and I will be with thee, and will bless thee; for unto thee, and unto thy seed, I will give all these countries, and I will perform the oath which I sware unto Abraham thy father;* (Genesis 26:3). The word Isaac passes to Jacob and his sons in Jasher is the word Yahuah (the Lord) first spoke to Isaac himself in Genesis: to your seed I will give this land, and I will perform the oath I swore to Abraham your father. Isaac does not hand it on as a bare deed; he hands it on with its condition in the open, if your children keep my statutes and my ways, and in the next verse he tells Jacob to teach his children and his children's children to fear Yahuah (the Lord). The land, the oath, and the keeping of his ways are passed down together from Abraham to Isaac to Jacob.
member_note: Jasher 47:7 — *To your seed will I give this land for an inheritance if your children keep my statutes and my ways.* Isaac hands Jacob the land oath Yahuah (the Lord) spoke to him in Genesis 26:3, with the keeping of his statutes attached.

new_note: *And Joseph did all these things, and made these statutes, in order that he might know when his brethren should come to Egypt to buy corn; and Joseph’s people caused it daily to be proclaimed in Egypt according to these words and statutes which Joseph had commanded.* (Jasher 50:37). *And Joseph was the governor over the land, and he it was that sold to all the people of the land: and Joseph’s brethren came, and bowed down themselves before him with their faces to the earth.* (Genesis 42:6). Jasher explains why Joseph set up his statutes for the sale of corn: so that he would know the moment his brethren came down to Egypt to buy. Genesis gives the moment itself, Joseph the governor selling to all the people of the land, and his brethren coming in and bowing before him with their faces to the earth. The sheaves of his boyhood dream bow at last, and Jasher shows it was not chance that brought them before him but a net Joseph had spread across all Egypt for that very day.
member_note: Jasher 50:37 — *in order that he might know when his brethren should come to Egypt to buy corn.* Joseph's statutes for the corn sale are laid so that the bowing of his brethren in Genesis 42:6 comes before his own face.

new_note: *At that time Jacob commanded his sons and household to go to Egypt according to the word of Yahuah (the Lord) to him, and Jacob rose up with his sons and all his household, and he went out from the land of Canaan from Beersheba, with joy and gladness of heart, and they went to the land of Egypt.* (Jasher 55:5). *And Yashar’el (Israel) went into the country of Egypt, 2172 A M. into the land of Goshen, on the new moon of the fourth month, in the second year of the third week of the forty-fifth jubilee.* (Jubilees 45:1). Jasher tells the going down: at the word of Yahuah (the Lord), Jacob rose with his sons and all his household and went out from Beersheba with joy and gladness of heart to the land of Egypt. Jubilees fixes the date of that same journey, the new moon of the fourth month in the year 2172, when Yashar'el (Israel) went into Goshen. One witness carries the heart of the old man leaving Canaan; the other carries the calendar, and together they set the beginning of the sojourn in Egypt on a day that can be counted.
member_note: Jasher 55:5 — *he went out from the land of Canaan from Beersheba, with joy and gladness of heart.* Jacob's going down from Beersheba to Egypt is the journey Jubilees 45:1 dates to the new moon of the fourth month.

new_note: *And behold Jacob ran and hastened to his son Joseph and fell upon his neck and kissed him, and they wept, and Joseph also embraced his father and kissed him, and they wept and all the people of Egypt wept with them.* (Jasher 55:15). *And Joseph made ready his chariot, and went up to meet Yashar'el (Israel) his father, to Goshen, and presented himself unto him; and he fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.* (Genesis 46:29). Jasher gives the meeting of Genesis in fuller motion: Jacob runs to Joseph and falls on his neck and kisses him, Joseph embraces and kisses his father, and all Egypt weeps with them. Genesis keeps the same falling on the neck and the long weeping, and adds the chariot made ready and the presenting of himself to Yashar'el (Israel) his father in Goshen. Twenty-two years of grief end on a neck in Goshen, and the next verse of Jasher gives Jacob's words, that now he can die cheerfully having seen Joseph's face.
member_note: Jasher 55:15 — *Jacob ran and hastened to his son Joseph and fell upon his neck and kissed him.* Jacob falling on Joseph's neck in Jasher is the meeting in Goshen of Genesis 46:29.
